title: Box 7.03 Reporting criteria for colorectal cancer
copyright: Adapted from WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Digestive system tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2019. (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 1). https://publications.iarc.who.int/579.
tablehtml:
Essential reporting criteria:

·    Histological subtype

·    Differentiation grade: Low/high

·    Invasion depth: According to TNM, specify if invasion in other organs (pT4) or tumour perforation

·    Presence of (lympho)vascular invasion: Intramural vascular invasion, extramural vascular invasion, lymphatic invasion

·    Perineural growth: Present/absent

·    Tumour budding status

·    Resection margin status (proximal, distal, circumferential): Positive, negative, distance in millimetres

·    Diameter of the tumour

·    Site/localization of the tumour

·    Quality of the resection specimen

·    Number of investigated lymph nodes

·    Number of positive lymph nodes

·    Presence of treatment response: Yes/no; if yes, partial or complete response

Desirable reporting criteria:

·    Microsatellite status / presence of DNA mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2): Microsatellite-stable or -unstable, staining for mismatch repair proteins present or absent

·    Immune response

·    Presence or absence of relevant mutations

Figure Panel E

diagnosis: Summary of colorectal cancer (CRC) molecular pathology classification systems
legend: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TGCA) DNA-based classification {670} distinguishes chromosomal instability (CIN) (84%), hypermutation due to deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) (13%), and ultramutation due to mutations in proofreading exonuclease domains (POLE and POLD1) (3%). The RNA-based consensus molecular subtypes classification {1642} uses four major groups: CMS1 (14%, microsatellite instability [MSI]-immune), CMS2 (37%, canonical), CMS3 (13%, metabolic), and CMS4 (23%, mesenchymal), with a residual mixed features or transitional group (13%). CMS1 correlates strongly with the TCGA hypermutation group (yellow arrows indicate dMMR/MSI CRC across the different classification systems). The large TCGA CIN group splits into the three remaining CMS groups. The colorectal intrinsic subtypes classification {1196} is based on epithelial neoplastic cells only (without stromal and immune cells), forming five subtypes: CRIS-A (24%), CRIS-B (11%), CRIS-C (24%), CRIS-D (15%), and CRIS-E (14%), with a non-classified residual group (12%). The single-cell intrinsic consensus molecular subtype classification {2166A} is based on single-cell transcriptomes and results in two intrinsic subtypes, iCMS2 (47%) and iCMS3 (42%), which refined the earlier CMS classification. iCMS3 contains the CMS1 dMMR/MSI cancers as well as one third of microsatellite-stable (MSS) CRCs. The pathway-derived subtypes classification {2987} distinguishes three subtypes, PDS1 (26%), PDS2 (31%), and PDS3 (30%), with a small residual PDS mixed group (13%), based on gene ontology–inferred pathway activation patterns. BRAFm, BRAF mutation; CIMP, CpG island methylator phenotype (-H, high or -L, low); EMT, epithelial–mesenchymal transition; CBC crypt base columnar stem cell populations; MLH1-s, silencing of MLH1 protein expression by promoter hypermethylation; SCNA, somatic copy-number alteration (-H, high or -L, low); TILs, tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes. Box heights indicate approximate relative proportion of CRC in each subgroup.
